dedupe_keys.name: climate forced hydropower simulations for brazil colombia and peru using nasa nex gddp

description: This data set gives simulated future usable capacity of hydropower plants in Brazil, Colombia and Peru under climate change, to characterise how climate uncertainty affects hydropower in South America. It was published in 2020 by Ana Lucia Caceres, Paulina Jaramillo, H. Scott Matthews, Constantine Samaras and Bart Nijssen, based on their study of Brazilian, Colombian and Peruvian plants under climate scenarios. Simulations were forced with NASA's Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP), using maximum and minimum temperature and precipitation from 21 global climate models for a retrospective run (1950 to 2005) and RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 projections. Each country folder has a plant characteristics file listing installed capacity, effective height and reservoir specifications, and usable capacity files per plant and scenario, with a separate folder of dates. Coverage is the hydropower fleets of three countries. Files are ZIP archives, about 52 MB, downloadable from Zenodo (version 1.1, December 2020) under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the update corrected values for Peruvian plants, and results depend on the hydrology model chain. Simulation uses are climate adaptation and drought risk screening for hydropower-dependent systems. Related records: data-us-federal-hydropower-projections-cmip5 does the same for US federal plants.
